A brick sea-turtle — domed green slope-brick shell with hexagon tile-pattern, plate flippers angled mid-stroke, printed-eye head on a short neck, gliding on a clear rod across the upper frame.

A brick manta-ray — broad flat plate-wings in dark-grey with white underside angled mid-glide, a tile-tail trailing, printed-eye cephalic head, suspended on a clear rod overhead casting a built shadow.
A brick clownfish-school — a dozen small orange-and-white slope-and-wedge fish on clear rods at a matched drift-angle weaving around a modified-plant anemone, printed-eye tiles on the leaders.
A brick reef-shark — a sleek grey slope-brick body with a plate dorsal fin and tile tail, printed-gill detail, cruising mid-frame on a clear rod with a slight downward menace-tilt.
A brick octopus — a domed purple head-build with eight curved tentacle-bar-elements splayed across a coral ledge, printed-eye tiles, one tentacle reaching toward a nearby shell.
A brick seahorse-pair — two upright seahorses with curled tail-builds and crest-plates in yellow and coral, tails linked around a single green plant-stem, mid-bob on a clear rod.
A brick moon-jellyfish drift — three trans-clear and trans-light-blue dome bells with trailing bar-rod tentacles, suspended at staggered heights suspended up the trans-blue water column.
A brick dolphin-pod — three grey-slope dolphins with white belly plates arcing on clear rods at the trans-blue surface, mid-leap in a staggered line, the lead dolphin highest.
A brick pufferfish — a round studded sphere-build in tan and cream bristling with tooth-element spines, tiny plate fins, printed-eye tiles, hovering puffed mid-frame on a clear rod.
A brick moray-eel — a green segmented body of stacked round-bricks emerging from a coral-hole, jaw-element open wide, printed-eye tile, the coiled remainder hidden deep in the reef structure.
A brick hermit-crab — a small crab-build tucked into a SNOT-spiral shell of curved slopes, claw-elements raised defensively, scuttling across the tan-plate seafloor on short bar-leg elements.
A brick gull-flock — four white-and-grey gull-builds with angled plate-wings on clear rods wheeling above the waterline, one tilted mid-dive beak-first toward the surface foam plates.
A brick orca — a large black-and-white slope-brick body with a tall plate dorsal fin, white eye-patch tile, plate flukes angled upward, surging on a clear rod at the surface.
A brick sea-otter — a tan plate-brick body floating belly-up at the surface, short claw-element paws clasping a round tile shellfish, printed-eye face resting against a kelp-stem build.
A brick stingray — a wide diamond plate-build in sandy tan with a long bar-rod tail, printed-eye tile on the underside, gliding low on a clear rod just above the seafloor.
A brick anglerfish — a dark trans-black and gunmetal slope-brick body with a hinge-jaw element gaping, a glowing trans-yellow lure on a curved bar overhead, suspended deep on a clear rod.
A brick crab — a flat dark-red plate body with six bar-leg elements spread wide, two oversized clip-claw arms raised, printed-eye tiles, posed sideways across a studded rock-plate ledge.
A brick lobster — a deep-red segmented body of stacked modified plates, long antenna-bar elements forward, large claw-elements snapping, printed-eye tiles, perched on a coral-base build at mid-frame.

A brick sea-anemone with clownfish — a column of stacked round-bricks topped with splayed plant-element tentacles in orange and white, two small wedge-built clownfish nestled inside on short clear rods.
A brick starfish-cluster — five orange five-pointed starfish built from plate-and-slope arms radiating from a central round tile, arranged at varied tilts across the sandy tan-plate shallows.
A brick hammerhead shark — a wide flat hammer-head of plate-extensions flanking a slope-brick snout, printed-eye tiles at each wing-tip, sleek grey body on a clear rod banking through mid-water.

A brick nudibranch — a flat elongated plate-body in bright trans-pink with stud-bump cerata along the spine, printed-eye tile, crawling slowly across a dark-grey rock-plate surface near the reef base.
A brick whale shark — a massive grey-and-white slope-brick body with white dot-tile spot pattern, wide plate mouth element open, gliding on two clear rods spanning the upper diorama frame.
A brick sea-snake — a yellow-and-black banded body of linked bar-and-connector segments undulating on a clear rod, small plate head with printed-eye tile, weaving between coral-stem builds.
A brick pelican — a white-and-grey plate-wing build with a long hinge-jaw beak element, printed-eye tile, perched on a barnacle-textured stud-brick piling above the waterline on the diorama edge.

A brick barracuda — a long narrow cylinder-brick body in silver-grey with a pointed wedge jaw-build, printed-gill tile, a forked plate-tail, suspended on a clear rod at a aggressive nose-down hunting angle.

A brick seahorse solo — a single tall upright seahorse in vivid lime-green with stacked round-plate body rings and a tightly curled tail-build gripping a coral-bar, crest-plates fanned, hovering mid-column.

A brick nautilus — a SNOT-built spiral shell of curved-slope segments in cream and brown stripes, tentacle-bar-elements fanning from the opening, printed-eye tile centered, suspended on a clear rod near the mid-column.

A brick whale-shark — a massive dark-blue slope-brick body speckled with round-white tile spots, a broad flat-plate mouth edge, plate pectoral fins swept back, cruising on a double clear-rod mount dominating the upper frame.

A brick seahorse lone — a single upright seahorse in pale-gold slope-bricks with a ridged plate-crest, curled tail-build locked around a pink coral-bar, printed-eye tile, suspended perfectly still on a clear rod mid-column.

A brick lionfish — a red-and-white striped slope-brick body with dramatic plate-spine fan-elements fanning above and below, tiny wedge fins, printed-eye tiles, hovering imperiously on a clear rod beside a coral-brick overhang.
A brick sea-lion — a sleek tan slope-brick body with short plate flippers, a whiskered printed-eye tile face, arching on a clear rod just above the trans-blue surface mid-roll.
A brick flying-fish — a silver slope-brick fish with broad trans-clear plate-wings extended flat, printed-eye tile, launched on a steep clear rod above the waterline in a low skimming arc.

A brick blue-tang — a flat disc-shaped blue slope-brick body with a yellow tail-plate and white-line printed tile flank, tiny plate pectoral fins, printed-eye tile, suspended on a clear rod weaving beside a coral-brick column.
